info.title: TRP WhatsApp Bot Reply API
info.description: Generates automated replies for Track Route Pro's WhatsApp bot.

post.description:
Create a new widget for a site. The returned `token` is what goes
in that site's <script> tag - keep it, it's how /widgets/{token}/...
below is addressed.

delete.description:
Permanently remove a widget: its config, its ENTIRE FAQ knowledge
base, and every uploaded file - use when a client's subscription
ends. This is irreversible; there's no undo. The token immediately
stops resolving anywhere (widget.js, /api/web/message, admin
endpoints all 404 for it afterwards), so an already-embedded script
tag on the client's site simply stops working rather than erroring
loudly - worth telling the client to remove the tag too.

post.description:
Store a file to link on one specific FAQ answer, without indexing
its content as its own searchable entry - same idea as the WhatsApp
bot's /faq/files/attach.

schema.title: Response Widget Faq List Sources Widgets  Token  Faq Sources Get

get.description:
Full detail for ONE FAQ - answer text and keywords included,
unlike the plain listing above (FAQSourceResponse deliberately only
carries title/attachment/type, since that's all a list table needs).
This is what an edit form actually needs to pre-fill correctly.

put.description:
Edit an existing FAQ in place - same id afterwards, unlike the old
delete-then-recreate approach (see FAQStore.update_source's docstring
for why that was a real problem, not just an inconvenience).

post.description:
Called when a visitor clicks one of the options from a previous
/api/web/message's `options` list - returns that exact FAQ's answer
directly, no text search involved.

Register a new WhatsApp number with this service. `phone_number_id`
must be Meta's own id for the number (visible in the WhatsApp Business
Platform setup, and in every inbound webhook's metadata) - it's what
every other endpoint below is addressed by, exactly like a widget's
token. Call this once per client number, before sending it any
messages or adding its FAQs.

schema.title: Response List Whatsapp Numbers Whatsapp Numbers Get

delete.description:
Permanently remove a WhatsApp number: its config, its ENTIRE FAQ
knowledge base, its bot persona config, and every uploaded file - use
when a client's subscription ends. Irreversible. Mirrors
widget_routes.py's delete_widget exactly.

post.description:
Store a file to link on one specific FAQ answer, without indexing
its content as its own searchable entry - same idea as main.py's

get.description:
Full detail for ONE FAQ, for an edit form - mirrors
widget_routes.py's widget_faq_get_source.

put.description:
Edit an existing FAQ in place - same id afterwards. Mirrors
widget_routes.py's widget_faq_update_source exactly.

get.description: Liveness check - the Java service (or a load balancer) can poll this.
Current bot name, links, products, and canned reply text.

put.description:
Save new bot config (name / links / products / reply text).
Takes effect immediately on the next incoming message - no restart needed.

post.description: Reset bot config back to the built-in defaults.

Given an inbound WhatsApp message, return the bot's reply text.

Stateless: send the customer's phone number + message text (name and
history are optional), get back the reply text to send over WhatsApp.

Call this when a customer taps one of the options from a previous
ReplyResponse.options list (a WhatsApp Reply Button or List Message
selection). Returns that exact FAQ's answer directly - no text
search involved, since the tapped id already says exactly which one
they meant.

Upload a document (pdf, docx, pptx, xlsx, txt, md, csv) to index.

The file itself is saved and served back at /faq/files/... - by
default (send_as_link=True) the bot replies with a link to the whole
file rather than a pasted snippet, since for things like a wiring
diagram or a spec sheet, the file *is* the answer. Set
send_as_link=false if this document is more like a manual FAQ (its
extracted text should be pasted directly into the bot's reply).

Store a file purely to be linked as an attachment on a specific,
manually-written FAQ answer - unlike /faq/upload/document, this does
NOT extract or index the file's content, so it never becomes
independently searchable/answerable on its own. Use this when a file
is attached to one particular Question in the FAQ UI, so only that
exact question's answer links to it - not any message that happens to
resemble text buried inside the file.

get.description:
Serve an uploaded document's original file so the bot can link to
the whole thing instead of pasting an extracted snippet.

Looked up by source_id alone (it's already a unique 8-char id per
upload) rather than requiring the filename in the URL to match the
stored filename byte-for-byte - filesystems are case-sensitive and
a client-side case change (browser, copy/paste, retyping) would
otherwise 404 even though the file genuinely exists.

post.description: Fetch a website URL and index its visible text.

Fetch a YouTube video's transcript and index it. Other video
platforms aren't supported - see extractors.py docstring for why.

Index raw text directly - the fallback for social media captions/
posts, or any manually-written FAQ content.

schema.title: Response Faq List Sources Faq Sources Get

delete.description: Remove a source (and all its chunks) from the index.

post.description:
Search the FAQ index for the best-matching content for a query.

Returns the top matching chunks plus a convenience `answer` field set
to the single best match's text when there's a confident match (or
null if nothing cleared the relevance threshold).

get.description:
Serve a file attached via company_faq_attach_file() above.

This route was simply missing - company_faq_attach_file() has
always handed back a URL pointing here
(/company/{company_id}/faq/files/{file_id}/{filename}), but nothing
ever answered a GET to it, so every FAQ attachment added for a
WhatsApp number (via FaqApiService::attachFile(), see
FaqController.php) was a dead link: the bot's reply correctly
included "Attachment: <url>", but opening that url 404'd. Mirrors
faq_get_file()'s existing single-tenant version and
widget_faq_get_file() in widget_routes.py, just scoped to this
company's own faq_files directory.

source_url.description: Link back to the original video/page/post/file, if one exists

send_as_link.title: Send As Link
send_as_link.description: If true, the bot's reply is just source_url rather than the text

id.title: Id
id.description: Pass this to /bot/faq/select when the customer taps this option

title.title: Title
title.description: Short label - keep under ~24 characters, WhatsApp truncates longer titles

description.title: Description
description.description: Full question text (up to ~72 characters) - use as a WhatsApp List Message row's description so the complete question is visible even when `title` is truncated

FAQOption.title: FAQOption
FAQOption.description:
One tappable option in an ambiguous-match reply - the calling app
(whatever sends the actual WhatsApp message) turns a list of these
into a WhatsApp interactive message: a List Message is the right fit
here (not Reply Buttons), since WhatsApp caps button titles at 20
characters with no room for a second field - a List Message row has
both a `title` (still short) and a `description` (up to ~72 chars),
so the full question is always visible even when `title` alone had
to be truncated. `id` is what comes back when the customer taps one -
pass it to POST /bot/faq/select to get that option's exact answer.

top_k.title: Top K
top_k.description: Max number of matching chunks to return

answer.title: Answer
answer.description: Best-match answer text if a confident match was found, else null

source_id.title: Source Id
source_id.description: The `id` from the FAQOption the customer tapped

text.title: Text
text.description: Raw text to index, e.g. a pasted social media caption or manual FAQ entry

name.title: Name
name.description: Friendly name for this source, e.g. 'Instagram post - return policy'

source_url.title: Source Url
source_url.description: Link back to the original post/page, e.g. the Instagram/Facebook/TikTok post URL. Included in the bot's reply when this source answers a question.

send_as_link.title: Send As Link
send_as_link.description: If true, the bot replies with just source_url instead of the text. Defaults to true only when source_url is set, false otherwise.

keywords.title: Keywords
keywords.description: Explicit keywords this FAQ should also match on. Also used to detect when two FAQs share a keyword, so the bot can show both instead of silently picking one.

link_text.title: Link Text
link_text.description: Display label for source_url, e.g. 'Click here' or 'View pricing'. Only meaningful alongside source_url - ignored if source_url isn't set. When absent, the raw URL is shown instead.

attachment_url.title: Attachment Url
attachment_url.description: A separately-uploaded file's URL for this FAQ, distinct from source_url/link_text. Storing this apart from source_url is what lets a FAQ have BOTH a manually-typed hyperlink AND an attached file at once - previously there was only one URL slot per FAQ, so setting one silently discarded the other. Included in the bot's reply alongside the answer (and the hyperlink, if also set) whenever it's present.

url.title: Url
url.description: Website URL to fetch and index

name.title: Name
name.description: Friendly name for this source; defaults to the URL

url.title: Url
url.description: YouTube video URL to transcribe and index

name.title: Name
name.description: Friendly name for this source; defaults to the URL

HistoryItem.title: HistoryItem
HistoryItem.description: One prior message, optionally sent for context. Not required.

key.title: Key
key.description: Short id used for matching, e.g. 'sentinel'

keywords.title: Keywords
keywords.description: Extra words that should also match this product, e.g. ['maglock', 'securelink']

message.title: Message
message.description: The inbound message text from the customer

profile_name.title: Profile Name
profile_name.description: Customer's WhatsApp profile name, if known

conversation_id.title: Conversation Id
conversation_id.description: Java-side conversation/message id, echoed back for log correlation only

history.title: History
history.description: Optional recent messages for context, oldest first. Safe to omit.

ReplyRequest.title: ReplyRequest
ReplyRequest.description: What the Java service sends for every inbound WhatsApp message.

example.message: What is the price of Sentinel?

reply.title: Reply
reply.description: Text to send back to the customer over WhatsApp. When `options` is also set, send this as the interactive message's body text, with `options` as the buttons/list - don't send `reply` as a second, separate plain-text message.

should_handoff_to_human.title: Should Handoff To Human
should_handoff_to_human.description: If true, a human agent should take over this conversation (bot reply can still be sent first)

options.title: Options
options.description: When set (2-3 items), several FAQs matched closely and the customer should be shown tappable options instead of one flattened answer. Send as WhatsApp Reply Buttons (<=3 options) or a List Message (more). When null, send `reply` as plain text as before - nothing else changes for every other message type (greeting, pricing, a single confident FAQ match, etc).

ReplyResponse.title: ReplyResponse
ReplyResponse.description: What this API sends back. The Java service sends `reply` to WhatsApp.

example.reply: Sentinel (wired GPS tracker) is available at a special price of Rs. 1,999 (MRP Rs. 5,999). More details: https://trpgps.com/product/trackroutepro-sentinel/

session_id.title: Session Id
session_id.description: Client-generated id (e.g. a UUID kept in localStorage) - not currently used server-side, reserved for future conversation history

escalated.title: Escalated
escalated.description: True when nothing in the knowledge base answered - widget can prompt for contact info / a human follow-up

options.title: Options
options.description: When set (2-3 items), several FAQs matched closely - render these as clickable buttons instead of showing `reply` as-is. When null, show `reply` normally as before.

id.title: Id
id.description: Pass this to /widget/{token}/faq/select when the visitor clicks this option

title.title: Title
title.description: Full question text - no truncation needed in a browser UI

WebOption.title: WebOption
WebOption.description:
One clickable option in an ambiguous widget reply - unlike
WhatsApp's FAQOption, a browser button has no character limit, so
`title` carries the full question as-is.

source_id.title: Source Id
source_id.description: The `id` from the WebOption the visitor clicked

message.title: Message
message.description: The inbound message text from the customer

profile_name.title: Profile Name
profile_name.description: Customer's WhatsApp profile name, if known

conversation_id.title: Conversation Id
conversation_id.description: Caller-side conversation/message id, echoed back for log correlation only

history.title: History
history.description: Optional recent messages for context, oldest first. Safe to omit.

WhatsAppBotReplyRequest.title: WhatsAppBotReplyRequest
WhatsAppBotReplyRequest.description:
Same shape as ReplyRequest, scoped to one WhatsApp number's own
knowledge base/config instead of the shared global one.

source_id.description: The `id` from the FAQOption the customer tapped

phone_number_id.description: Meta's phone_number_id for this WhatsApp Business number - from the WhatsApp Business Platform setup, and present in every inbound webhook's metadata.phone_number_id. This is this number's key everywhere below, like a widget's token.
